scope: Brief reading summaries of current final.md; not replacement chapters

summaries.summary: A running number and a movable “you” introduce a world already underway, asking what we inherit when we choose where to count from.
An invisible point acquires a visible sphere and a physical boundary, exposing separate decisions behind what a body can see, approach and touch.
Carrying a sphere between local and world readings makes position situated, asking how measurement and permission shape where a body can arrive.
Moving endpoints, crossing a beam and following drawn routes turn lines into measures and directions, asking what a journey needs beyond its endpoints.
A hand, pen or rolling ball leaves a selected record of movement; bringing the trace into the next hall lets that finished gesture become a sculpture and find another use.
The trace arrives as a sculpture. Different displayed versions retain partial accounts of the hand’s movement; keeping the source allows another use without erasing it.
Three chosen corners become a boundary and a visible face through different instructions. Connectivity is a decision about belonging and order, while seeing a surface does not yet make it solid.
Open corners become enclosed volumes, barriers and slopes, asking how a geometric boundary differs from admitting a body or suggesting its direction.
Moving cube corners and unfolding hinged faces expose different constructions beneath a familiar shape, asking what must stay connected for recognition to survive.

Ordered solids and a family of cylinders make the desire for geometry tangible. Choosing a rule changes how we make and know the positions, while particular surfaces and differences remain available to inspection.
Supplied meshes, letters and resting trails reveal the engine’s inherited vocabulary, asking which choices we accept when a ready-made form becomes an object.
Columns vary profile, height and sampling separately, asking whether more divisions serve the silhouette, facets and relationships we actually want to keep.
Letter outlines become bodies resembling doorways and vessels, exposing inherited contours and asking what changes when a readable opening becomes bodily space.
Progressively rounded rings and a staged pursuit approach limits without reaching them, asking when a finite construction gives enough to continue.
An arrangement of tools and forms holds geometry beside the unfinished work of making. Knowing how to construct a cube does not choose its place or tell us what the arrangement should mean.
Four cubes accumulate rising, turning and swelling before becoming pickups, asking which properties remain recognisable through different kinds of movement.
Moving, growing and turning platforms offer timed crossings over fire, asking how the same geometric operation grants passage within someone else’s duration.
Carriers connect islands while differently constrained mechanisms share destinations, asking how journeys can reach the same place with different permissions to move.
Turning crossings and articulated forms expose pivots, order and release rules, asking what returns to the same pose and who controls the journey.
An enlarging furnished room and an adjustable doorway change what fits, asking whose body supplies the measure when geometry scales but experience does not.
Slats, a cut lattice and blocks answer the visitor’s approach differently, asking which boundaries return and which retain a record of contact.
Translating blocks, turning slabs and growing cubes close familiar ground, while a responsive door makes welcome depend on chosen reach, width and waiting time.
Repeated cubes acquire addresses, vacancies and bounded variation, asking what belongs to a slot and what bodily permissions an indexed arrangement cannot supply.
Flight opens a volume of indexed cubes while collection leaves vacancies, asking how addressing, reaching and keeping a record describe different kinds of presence.
One triangular motif receives different turns across six floors, asking how shared rules produce resemblance and what one addressed exception can change.
Floor patterns become tall walls and an opening, asking how scale, viewpoint and physical support alter what the same repeated image lets us see and do.
A changing checkerboard and a sequencer give fixed addresses timed events, separating the pattern’s returning beat from the visitor’s freedom to move.
Familiar forms gather into coloured stacks, asking how a changed palette rearranges relations between parts, their surroundings and what a composition recalls.
Movable coloured lamps and changing rooms separate light from material, asking how a visible patch depends on the meeting that produces it.
A colour selector dresses small and monumental hands, asking how the same numerical choice changes meaning when it colours nails or skin.
Alternative rainbow arrangements and repeatable confetti make room for celebration, asking how ordered colours and rewards can offer participation without requiring obedience.
A walkable field of coloured pillars gives hue, saturation and value spatial addresses, asking what sampled bodies omit and colour alone cannot recover.
A selected floor square keeps a chosen colour until a rule replaces it, asking what an address preserves when its previous value disappears.
An automatic spray can and the visitor’s hand share an evolving canvas, asking what a surface retains of movements it does not keep separate.
Coloured partitions and rearrangeable structures change the view as visitors move, asking which display accommodations and powers to alter a room remain hidden.
A familiar checkerboard changes palette and pattern while a score repeats, asking how the same floor can invite movements it never records.
Looms, stamps and pattern instruments dress the architecture, asking how far one mark travels and which copies can keep an earlier version.
Two fields repeat the same editable source differently, asking how an asymmetric mark reveals reversals that a symmetrical image can conceal.
A repeated mark wraps a walkable passage, asking how cell size, surface directions and seams affect the meaning of an address.
An asymmetric mark tests named symmetry rules beside a held comparison, asking what classification explains and what a finite carpet or garment leaves outside it.
A coloured array extends into a volume and selected slices, asking how stored values become bodies and what a revealing reduction withholds.
Equal colour values meet different neighbours, materials and curved supports, asking how a carrier participates in the appearance of the pattern it receives.
A repeated mark moves onto garments and a procession, asking what appearance can carry between bodies while deformation, collision and material retain different conditions.
Sampled curves, accumulated rectangles and a returning bridge compare descriptions of change, asking what intervals keep and what a net result leaves out.
Particles trace routes through a held field, asking how similar swirls can conceal different rules and apparent company can exist without mutual influence.
Movable pins and wall arrows separate position, difference and direction, asking what two movements can share without making their starting conditions identical.
A carriage follows two joined displacements and can return home, asking how a journey can add up to no change of position.
An alignment console calls agreement friendship, while a projection keeps only part of a gap, asking which relations measurements admit or leave aside.
A launch curve surrounds the visitor, asking how starting velocity, local time and an observation boundary shape a flight whose landing response remains unanswered.
A cube keeps moving after its push ends and meets a selective boundary, asking how retained velocity and different permissions shape a shared room.
Two bodies receive the same field through different movement rules, asking why one approaches a centre while another carries its velocity through it.
Cubes cross air, water and honey while other instruments annotate work, asking which arrows cause motion and why returning does not undo a journey.
A released spring carries its cube through the resting line, asking how restoration, retained motion and parameter changes determine what coming back means.
Turning rods, parcel deliveries and coupled clocks return at different rates, asking whose expectation determines whether simultaneous processes count as working together.
An orbiting pair gains a moving centre and a third body, asking who gets to stay still and where a bounded observation ends.
A plate settles onto supports beside a predicted footprint, asking how contact sustains a body and why a persuasive walking shape may lack support.
A creature changes direction and state around food while carts collide, asking how visible behaviour invites interpretations beyond the relationships actually implemented.
A plank and a configurable field offer ways across a hole, asking how an instruction becomes different consequences for a visitor and a cube.
A point steps downhill across an authored landscape, asking how starting position, stopping tolerance and a chosen cost determine what counts as improvement.
Hand-shaped cables, evaluated curves and film references compare routes to form, asking which boundaries and allowed changes make an answer possible.
Cloth, a lattice and a vessel retain repeated corrections, asking how stiffness, constraints and a finite computation budget leave their choices in a shape.
A calculated balance and apparently stable structures ask how to distinguish forces that cancel from a convincing image of something holding still.
A search accepts worse steps to leave a valley, while contrasting wells ask whether reaching the lowest score preserves the responsiveness a form needs.
Loose pieces can form a quiet heap the detector rejects, asking how chosen recognition rules separate a stable result from a shape that counts.
A hand-released pendulum and two returning cubes distinguish state from a clock, asking what a repeated crossing retains and what its count cannot show.
A swing leaves marks travelling down the hall, asking how sampling and display turn past movement into space while deciding how much history survives.
Spheres meet a folded wave surface while moving walls layer returning shapes, asking how contact, viewpoint and phase give similar forms different consequences.
A circling point leaves sampled projections as a graph, asking what a single height cannot recover about direction, phase and a continuing cycle.
A lattice spreads motion through neighbouring oscillators, asking how a travelling pattern emerges from bodies that remain in place and what disconnection reveals.
Two movable controls let one wave alter another’s note, asking what listening reveals when a scaled display conceals changes in the relationship.
Twisted columns rotate beside a repeating voice, separating movement built into a shape from motion in time and asking what a returning “now” means.
A drone and intermittent sounds invite attention to unpredictable intervals, asking how chance changes a composition within an authored vocabulary it cannot exceed.
Striking metal bars starts notes that outlast contact, asking how gesture, stored sound and a brief waveform display keep different parts of the event.
A sampled curve becomes turning treads and connecting surfaces, asking what provision a mathematical route needs for bodies with different strides.
Two quick oscillations produce a slow beat or a drawn figure, asking how their relationship becomes visible through different ways of combining them.
Five harmonic sliders and a repeating voice recording compare kinds of return, asking what a recipe retains and what an evolving result changes.
Two coloured grids replay unfamiliar arrangements from seeds, asking what must be kept for a surprising result to return and what can remain unexamined.
Tiles, counts and an entropy gauge describe the same record differently, asking what a persuasive number forgets about order, neighbours and eligible choices.
Amber candidates and disappearing floor cells reveal a set chosen before the draw, asking who is excluded from a supposedly fair random choice.
Two diagonal marks become printed fields, walls and an ant’s world, asking when an arrangement becomes a contour, a barrier or a passage.
A thrown die earns a spectacle and repeated throws gather into records, asking how reward rules and counting make some outcomes seem more consequential.
Wear, accumulating random turns and a fixed sine arrangement resemble disorder differently, asking what a changing surface reveals about a history that leaves no trail.
Beads leave bounded trails while visits build terrain, asking how an apparent destination or creature can exceed the memory and relations a movement rule possesses.
Falling samples gather beneath an expected curve while a painted centre stays empty, asking what counting, clipping and rejection conceal about where values belong.
A mushroom population and changing garments give sampled values authored bodies, asking which differences a recipe admits and what another possibility would require.
Independent and related column heights invite landscape readings, asking what neighbouring values actually share before colour and perception supply an imagined geological history.
Painting, pipes, particles and a dartboard give chance different jobs, asking what each procedure permits randomness to change and what its record retains.
Walkers leave scent and raised terrain that remember visits differently, asking how attraction or avoidance turns a previous passage into influence on the next.
Layered fields resemble land without retaining visits or settings, asking how colour and normalisation supply differences a landscape reading can mistake for history.
Disappearing stones and differently disclosed passages put uncertainty underfoot, asking which decisions precede choice and what a visitor can know before committing.
A constrained point, needle heights and sound rules locate variation in different relationships, asking which rules keep acting after a form has appeared.
Three related columns change through different operations, asking how an existing body receives variation and whether its appearance can reveal where change enters.
Two rings receive the same field as relief and colour, asking how a shared value becomes different surfaces, movements and possibilities for contact.
A threshold removes blocks while the sampled field remains fixed, asking what a yes-or-no boundary makes available and which differences it discards.
Layered clouds dress an inner room and sphere, asking how sums, colour and display limits create apparent depth without giving the body another foothold.
An enclosing sphere and paired probes show one field borrowing another’s coordinates, asking how changed addresses rearrange a body without changing the underlying seed.
Two proposed routes cross the same adjustable terrain, asking how a changed surface or chosen path alters what the ground can offer a body.
Paired fields, arches and a moving sheet compare generators, asking what must be held steady before a visible difference can support an explanation.
A turning sphere leaves space to revisit one remembered encounter, asking how naming an operation helps inquiry without deciding what the experience was worth.
Graphs and a moving wave expose rules written directly on coordinates and time, asking why a changed setting jumps when no past state is kept.
Repeated shapes and apparently matched seams reveal address rules beneath ornament, asking when a persuasive surface hides the boundary it seems to explain.
Five turning bodies answer to eye angle, lamps and shape, asking what their responsive surfaces notice and what a visitor cannot change.
Glass carries the visitor above moving water and layered noise studies, asking how visible depth, remembered state and the surface underfoot differ.
Emissive bodies and ankle-deep rendered water exaggerate familiar materials, asking what a surface answers to and whether changeable parts promise freedom beyond their menu.
A uniformly green square and branching frost question their labels, asking what a pattern needs before its next frame can inherit an actual past.
A waiting row and a changing rug compare local updates, asking what cells hold, which neighbours count and when a new answer becomes available.
A three-state volume lets activity linger before disappearing, asking how stored past, neighbours and empty boundaries decide where another beginning becomes possible.
One stored history appears as bars, a floor and a lattice, asking how time becomes inhabitable space and why a gap changes meaning underfoot.
A glider returns at new addresses while cells start and stop, asking what travels when a recognisable body has no moving object of its own.
A path weakens near the visitor and recovers through neighbours, asking which stored values and update choices let a surface carry a body.
Paired fields send different amounts into a marked cell and dress curved walls, asking what a neighbourhood supplies and what its coloured image conceals.
A local rule’s triangular history resembles a recursively built pyramid, asking where visual correspondence ends and why a pattern’s name does not prove its capabilities.
Almost matching volumes follow one altered value through shared rules, asking how storage precision changes the differences that neighbours can retain and pass onward.
